subject: english-language
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Paper 2 structure and assessment (Writers' Viewpoints and Perspectives)
Section A: Reading — one non-fiction and one literary non-fiction text
Comparing writers' ideas and perspectives across texts (AO3)
Analysing writers' use of language and structure (AO2)
Section B: Writing — present a viewpoint (AO5/AO6)

questions.q: How long is the AQA GCSE English Language Paper 2 examination?
questions.explain: Paper 2 is a written exam lasting 1 hour 45 minutes.

questions.q: What is the total number of marks available on Paper 2?
questions.explain: Paper 2 carries 80 marks in total, split evenly between reading and writing.

questions.q: What percentage of the overall GCSE English Language grade does Paper 2 represent?
questions.explain: Paper 2 is worth 50% of the GCSE, the same as Paper 1.

questions.q: How many marks are available for Section A (Reading) on Paper 2?
questions.explain: Section A (Reading) and Section B (Writing) are each worth 40 marks.

questions.q: How many source texts do students read in Section A of Paper 2?
questions.explain: Section A presents two linked source texts for reading and comparison.

questions.q: From which time periods are the two Section A texts drawn?
options: One 19th-century text and one 20th- or 21st-century text
One medieval and one modern text
questions.explain: The paper pairs a 19th-century text with one from either the 20th or 21st century.

questions.q: Which assessment objective requires students to compare writers' ideas and perspectives across two or more texts?
questions.explain: AO3 assesses comparison of writers' ideas and perspectives and how these are conveyed.

questions.q: Which assessment objective covers analysing how writers use language and structure to achieve effects?
questions.explain: AO2 targets analysis of language and structure using relevant subject terminology.

questions.q: What kinds of texts are used in Section A of Paper 2?
questions.explain: Paper 2 focuses on non-fiction and literary non-fiction such as letters, articles, diaries and travel writing.

questions.q: The first Section A question (4 marks) typically asks students to do what?
options: Select true statements about a specified part of one text
questions.explain: Question 1 tests AO1 by asking students to identify true statements from a named section of Source A.

questions.q: The 8-mark question in Section A mainly requires students to do what?
options: Summarise differences using inferences and evidence from both texts
Analyse one writer's use of structure
questions.explain: This AO1 question tests selecting and synthesising evidence across both texts to summarise differences.

questions.q: The 12-mark question in Section A asks students to focus on what?
options: How the writer uses language for effect in one text
How to structure a persuasive letter
Which statements about a text are true
questions.explain: This AO2 question requires analysis of language and its effects in a single named source.

questions.q: The final 16-mark reading question requires students to compare what across both texts?
options: The writers' different perspectives and the methods used to convey them
Only the vocabulary used in each text
The historical accuracy of each text
questions.explain: The 16-mark AO3 question compares writers' viewpoints and how these attitudes are conveyed.

questions.q: When analysing language for AO2, students are expected to support their points using what?
questions.explain: AO2 rewards precise analysis supported by relevant subject terminology.

questions.q: In the mark scheme for the Section B writing task, what does AO5 assess?
questions.explain: AO5 assesses communication, matching form to purpose and audience, and organisation of ideas.

questions.q: What does AO6 assess in the Section B writing task?
options: Technical accuracy of vocabulary, sentences, spelling and punctuation
questions.explain: AO6 rewards a range of vocabulary and sentence structures with accurate spelling and punctuation.

questions.q: The Section B writing task on Paper 2 always asks students to do what?
options: Present a viewpoint on a given topic
questions.explain: Section B is a single writing task in which students present a point of view for a specified form, purpose and audience.

questions.q: A task reads: '"Homework should be banned." Write an article for a broadsheet newspaper explaining your point of view.' Which approach best meets the task?
options: Adopt the form and register of an article and present a clear, consistent viewpoint with persuasive techniques
Write a first-person narrative story about doing homework
Produce a bulleted list of reasons with no development
Describe a classroom scene in vivid sensory detail
questions.explain: AO5 rewards matching the article form and audience while presenting a sustained, persuasive viewpoint.

questions.q: Which sentence from a student's persuasive writing uses a rhetorical question?
options: Do we really want our children glued to screens all day?
Screens are used by children every single day.
I believe children use screens too much.
Children spend many hours looking at screens.
questions.explain: A rhetorical question is posed for effect rather than to gain an answer, engaging the reader directly.

questions.q: Source A (19th century) praises the excitement of railway travel, while Source B (modern) criticises the stress of commuting. For the 16-mark comparison, the strongest response would do what?
options: Compare both writers' contrasting attitudes and analyse the methods each uses to convey them
Summarise only what happens in Source A
Quote long passages from Source B without comment
Describe the writer's own train journey
questions.explain: AO3 requires comparing perspectives and the methods used to convey them, supported by evidence from both texts.

specSource: AQA GCSE English Language (8700) specification; Paper 2: Writers' Viewpoints and Perspectives
